(1) 3 days are necessary to reliably measure mean cortisol and A.U.C., and 5-10 days are required for slope; (2) 3 or 6 days of 2 samples per day are needed to assess mean and slope; and (3) 3 or more days of 4 samples per day are required for AUC.

(1) for between-person comparisons, 3 days of sampling (morning and evening saliva) is necessary to reliably estimate mean, slope, and AUC; and (2) for within-person comparisons, 10 days of sampling (6 morning and 4 evening saliva samples) is necessary to estimate slope reliably.

(1) to assess between-person diurnal cortisol differences, at least 4 days of data collection are necessary, (2) to assess within-person changes in cortisol, at least 5 days of data collection per occasion are necessary, (3) to assess diurnal slope, 5-8 data collection days are necessary, and (4) to assess diurnality, 3 data collection days are sufficient.
